qs.ours: Prov. xxiv. 27. ¦ *f* Plato (Repub. x.) compares pretenders to moral worth to those who set out briskly in a race, but soon flag, and retire with shame; and goes on to recommend very serious and deliberate consideration. Epictetus employs the 15th chapter of his 3d book in recommending the most careful weighing of the difficulties, before assuming the character of a philosopher, lest the result should be a disgraceful failure.
